M1.reason: The outline is a low, flat slab with one sloped end (side and top views, sides.png), a plain block about 21 x 4 x 31 units. A pump-action shotgun's barrel, receiver, pump, grip, trigger and folding stock do not show in any of the ten views. The silhouette does not match the brief's words, so it fails the outline test in all six views.

M2.reason: The longest measured side is 31.4 against the brief's 30, 4.7% over and within the 15% band (sizeOff 0.048). Length is the only size the brief gives, so the measure holds. It does not make the shape right, which M1 and M3 cover.

M3.reason: The brief names a pump, a folding stock with a hooked end, a trigger and guard, and a barrel. None of these is present. The asset has only a bevelled slab, and the front, side and attack views show no separate pump, stock, trigger or guard.

M4.reason: The whole asset is one mid-grey surface (sides.png, first-person.png). The brief asks for black metal and a wooden or dark pump, so the colour is clearly off. No separate region of wood or dark pump is there at all.

M5.reason: The only detail is a bevel highlight on the edges and diagonal shading streaks from the triangulation (sides.png, Top and Back-Left). The brief names no markings, but a pump-action shotgun's ribbing, slide and receiver lines are absent, and the streaks read as artefacts, not detail.

M6.reason: In lineup.png the asset (A, a grey wedge) is the first thing a player would not take for one of the game's. The line-up measure is consistent with that: the asset was picked as the non-Valve model twice in four readings (positions C and C), so it is caught at least twice and capped at 1. Visually it is a box, so it is scored 0.

M7.reason: No front is identifiable. The side views show a slab with a sloped end and no muzzle, stock or grip to show which way round it should face. It lies on its origin, as a dropped weapon would, but the facing cannot be checked against a shotgun's.

M8.reason: checkErrors is empty, the asset has 10 triangles (well under twice the median of 138), and its closed outline shows no open side, inside-out face or floating part in the ten views.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset sits in the left half of the view, while the game's shotgun sits in the right half. It is held at its base by the orange hand but is not shaped as a grip, so it is not held the way a shotgun is held. Through attack.png the hand stays at the bottom left and the slab moves away from it, so the attack reads as the weapon swinging out of the hand, not a gun being worked.
